thought.text: All authenticated endpoints are working. The QGIS OWS endpoint is up and responding, and it needs a MAP parameter. Let me check the contents of QGIS's /projects and try a MAP-based request. Also, I'll verify the database and frontend HTML.

reasoning_content:
Authenticated endpoints are working:
- auth/user: 200 with admin user
- projects: 200 with the "Default" project (created by load_initial_data)
- WebDAV PROPFIND: 200 multistatus XML
- QGIS: The OWS endpoint is responding, but it requires a MAP parameter pointing to a valid QGIS project. The documentation says the URL is `https://qgis.localhost/ows/?MAP=/projects/<project>.qgz` — the project file has to be placed on the QGIS server's filesystem. The summary notes that the bundled test-project.qgz is a 16-byte placeholder.

Let me check what's in the QGIS server's /projects directory, and try GetCapabilities with the MAP parameter. Also, let me check the database directly and check the frontend rendering.

action.command:
cd /workspace/deployment
TOKEN=$(cat /tmp/token.txt)
echo '=== qgis-server /projects ==='
docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml exec qgis-server ls -la /projects/ 2>&1
docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml exec qgis-server ls -la /projects/*/ 2>&1 | head
echo '=== WMS GetCapabilities with MAP=test-project ==='
curl -sk --resolve qgis.localhost:443:127.0.0.1 "https://qgis.localhost/ows/?SERVICE=WMS&REQUEST=GetCapabilities&MAP=/projects/test-project.qgz" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -o /tmp/wms_caps2.xml -w 'HTTP %{http_code} size=%{size_download}\n'
head -c 400 /tmp/wms_caps2.xml; echo
